title: Jacob's Last Words to His Sons
overview: Near death, Jacob speaks to each of his twelve sons in turn, in poetic sayings that look ahead to the tribes descended from them, and then he dies.

parts.label: Reuben, Simeon and Levi (vv. 1-7)
parts.note: Jacob's words look ahead to the tribes that will come from his sons. Reuben, the eldest, loses the leading place for sleeping with his father's secondary wife (Genesis 35), and Simeon and Levi are condemned for their massacre at Shechem (Genesis 34); later the Levites had no land of their own and Simeon's land lay inside Judah's.

parts.label: Judah the lion (vv. 8-12)
parts.note: Judah gets the leading role, and the lion and scepter (a king's rod) are usually read as pointing to King David's royal line, while the vines and wine picture lavish plenty. The Hebrew of verse 10 is unclear (one reading is "until Shiloh comes"), and Christians have traditionally read it as pointing to Jesus as the promised king.

parts.label: Zebulun through Naphtali (vv. 13-21)
parts.note: Short sayings fit each tribe: Zebulun toward the coast, Issachar trading freedom for good farmland, Dan (whose name sounds like "judge") as a cunning snake that can bring down a rider, Gad striking back at raiders, Asher's rich food, and Naphtali as a deer set free. The sudden prayer in verse 18 interrupts the list, and scholars are unsure why it sits there.

parts.label: Joseph and Benjamin (vv. 22-27)
parts.note: Joseph, the favorite, gets the longest blessing: a thriving vine, and archers who attacked him, likely recalling the hatred and suffering he survived with God's help. Benjamin, the youngest, is pictured as a wolf, fitting the fierce, warlike tribe known later in Israel's history.

parts.label: Burial wish and death (vv. 28-33)
parts.note: Jacob repeats his wish to be buried in the cave Abraham bought in Canaan, which many readers take as a sign that he tied his hopes to the land promised to his family rather than to Egypt. "Gathered to his people" is an old way of saying he died and joined his ancestors.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether verse 10 is a direct prediction of Jesus or first a statement about David's royal line that Christians later saw fulfilled in him.
think: Jacob's last words name some of his sons' worst moments alongside their strengths; what do you think it does to a family when old wrongs are spoken aloud at the end of a life?
